hyundai-kia-4wd.notes: The 4WD controller frames (_4WD11/_4WD12/_4WD13, node _4WD) of opendbc's hyundai_can.dbc plus the ABS wheel-speed frame they work against. opendbc defines but does not use these frames, so which models send them is unknown. The 2H/4H/LOW flags suggest the same frames also cover part-time transfer-case systems; the source does not say. No diagnostic channel is declared: no open source documents the 4WD unit's diagnostic ids. Signal meanings beyond the DBC names and scales are marked per signal.
safety: Changing how an AWD system engages changes how the car drives. OpenTune only decodes these frames; it never commands the coupling.
Do not transmit on a drivetrain CAN bus of a moving car: these frames feed the engine, brakes and instrument cluster. Log with a listen-only adapter.

params.description: Raw 4-byte bitfield: A7 = MIL on, A0-A6 = number of emission-related DTCs, B-D = readiness (monitor supported / incomplete) bits. Decode the bits; the numeric value itself is not a quantity.

obd2-mode01.source: SAE J1979 / ISO 15031-5 service 01 PID definitions (formulas as published in the standard; also tabulated at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OBD-II_PIDs)

obd2-functional.addr_note: A functional request reaches every OBD ECU; this entry listens only on 0x7E8 (ECU #1). Use obd2-physical.json to see each ECU separately.
obd2-functional.source: ISO 15765-4 (11-bit OBD-on-CAN identifiers); SAE J1979 / ISO 15031-5
obd2-functional.vehicle: Generic OBD-II — ISO 15765-4 functional broadcast (0x7DF, first reply on 0x7E8)

obd2-physical.addr_note: addr = low byte of the 11-bit request id (11-bit normal addressing has no separate logical address).
obd2-physical.source: ISO 15765-4 (11-bit OBD-on-CAN identifiers); SAE J1979 / ISO 15031-5

obd-clear-dtcs.description: WRITES TO THE ECU. Clears emission-related DTCs, freeze-frame data and test results, turns the MIL off and RESETS ALL READINESS MONITORS to 'incomplete' (the car may fail an inspection until they complete again). Engine off, ignition on. Only runs after the operator ticks the confirmation box. Mode 04 sent physically clears only the addressed ECU; use Auto-scan → Clear with obd2-physical.json to clear every OBD ECU. Defaults to OBD ECU #1 (0x7E0/0x7E8, ISO 15765-4); enter another ECU's ids in the Target fields to address it instead.
obd-clear-dtcs.name: OBD: clear DTCs and stored values (mode 04) — WRITE

obd-read-pending-dtcs.description: Read-only. Pending (current / last drive cycle) emission-related DTCs. Defaults to OBD ECU #1 (0x7E0/0x7E8, ISO 15765-4); enter another ECU's ids in the Target fields to address it instead.
obd-read-pending-dtcs.name: OBD: read pending DTCs (mode 07)

obd-read-permanent-dtcs.description: Read-only. Permanent DTCs (cannot be erased by mode 04; they clear themselves after the monitor passes). Not supported by older ECUs. Defaults to OBD ECU #1 (0x7E0/0x7E8, ISO 15765-4); enter another ECU's ids in the Target fields to address it instead.
obd-read-permanent-dtcs.name: OBD: read permanent DTCs (mode 0A)

obd-read-stored-dtcs.description: Read-only. Confirmed emission-related DTCs as 2-byte codes (CAN responses carry a leading count byte). Defaults to OBD ECU #1 (0x7E0/0x7E8, ISO 15765-4); enter another ECU's ids in the Target fields to address it instead.
obd-read-stored-dtcs.name: OBD: read stored DTCs (mode 03)

obd-read-vin.description: Read-only. Vehicle identification number; on CAN the response is `49 02 01` followed by 17 ASCII characters. Defaults to OBD ECU #1 (0x7E0/0x7E8, ISO 15765-4); enter another ECU's ids in the Target fields to address it instead.
obd-read-vin.name: OBD: read VIN (mode 09 InfoType 02)

obd-readiness.description: Read-only. Monitor status since DTCs cleared: byte A bit 7 = MIL on, bits 0-6 = DTC count; bytes B-D = which readiness monitors are supported and which are still incomplete. Defaults to OBD ECU #1 (0x7E0/0x7E8, ISO 15765-4); enter another ECU's ids in the Target fields to address it instead.
obd-readiness.name: OBD: read readiness / MIL status (mode 01 PID 01)

wot-pull.description: Records wide-open-throttle pulls from the SAE J1979 mode-01 channels and marks coolant over-temperature. Channel ids list the loggers/obd2-mode01.json id first and the `opentune obd read` key second, so the file works with both. Use: opentune obd read --driver <id> --rounds 0 --out pulls.csv --trigger packs/generic-obd2/triggers/wot-pull.json --split 0C 11 05
wot-pull.name: WOT pull + over-temperature marks (generic OBD-II)

triggers.description: Engine speed (PID 0x0C) above 3000 rpm with throttle position (PID 0x11) above 90 % for 300 ms. Released after 1 s below either threshold; keeps 3 s before the fire and 5 s after the release.
triggers.name: wot-pull

triggers.description: Coolant temperature (PID 0x05) above 105 °C for 1 s; re-arms after 5 s below.
triggers.name: coolant-hot
